headline: High-risk networked EMQX paired with offline Spring samples creates default data-exposure and workflow-conflict risks; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between emqx and spring-integration-samples. emqx exposes HTTP API and broad network egress, but spring-integration-samples has no io_surfaces or network egress, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is limited by missing interaction docs, but the pathway is not shown.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not connect them through clipboard or shared message queues.
Review any future bridge for provenance tagging.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: emqx touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples is docs-only and shows no local egress controls. If they share a workspace or EMQX forwards IoT payloads into Spring flows, sensitive data can move into outputs or external services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default integrations, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same workspace or queue, IoT payloads can be exposed to the second agent.
IF EMQX forwards message contents into Spring Integration flows, those contents may be logged or relayed.
mitigations: Separate data stores for each agent.
Disable payload logging on any shared integration path.
Restrict EMQX egress to approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared queues.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: emqx has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while spring-integration-samples shows no write or network capabilities. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct capability conflict is limited. If an operator later grants Spring write access to the same endpoints or files, conflict risk rises.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is given write access to the same external service or filesystem as emqx, conflicting updates become possible.
mitigations: Keep write scopes disjoint.
Avoid shared mutable queues.
Use explicit locking if both touch the same resource.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks on shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: emqx can emit networked outputs from IoT data, and spring-integration-samples is a workflow sample that could consume those outputs. If Spring treats EMQX messages as authoritative without verification, errors or malformed payloads can cascade into downstream actions. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Spring Integration consumes EMQX messages without schema validation, bad upstream data can propagate.
IF downstream handlers trigger actions from those messages, the cascade can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Add schema validation at the Spring boundary.
Require human review for action-triggering messages.
Log and quarantine malformed payloads.
requires-engineering: add replay-safe idempotency keys.
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata to EMQX outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: emqx touches IoT data and has broad network egress, but the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or residency constraints. spring-integration-samples has no data classes touched and no compliance-specific fields. Because no concrete mismatch is documented, compliance risk is limited to potential future deployment choices rather than the pair itself.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed through a non-compliant deployment of either agent, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or residency settings differ between the two deployments, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Confirm data classification before routing.
Disable unnecessary retention on both sides.
Keep regulated data out of the pair unless controls are added.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention policy alignment.
